row.scim_price_text: Sales Hub Professional: $90/seat/mo (billed annually) + $1,500 one-time onboarding
row.evidence: HubSpot's developer SCIM guide says 'This feature requires a HubSpot Professional or Enterprise account' and that SSO must be enabled; the Okta and Google SCIM articles and the SSO article are all marked 'Professional, Enterprise'.
row.notes: Status stays gated, but the gate moved down from Enterprise to Professional: SSO (required for SCIM) is now available on Professional and Enterprise of every hub, so June's 'SSO is Enterprise-only, effective requirement Enterprise at $150/seat/mo' no longer holds. Prices are taken from the Sales Hub page (the /pricing URL redirects to Marketing Hub): Starter $7/seat/mo billed annually (list $20 struck through), Professional $90/seat/mo billed annually ($100 monthly) plus a required one-time $1,500 Professional Onboarding, Enterprise $150/seat/mo plus $3,500 onboarding. Starter dropped from June's $20. Marketing Hub Professional is seat-bundled instead ($800/mo with 3 core seats). June's 'min 10 seats' Enterprise figure was not found on any first-party page and was dropped. Okta and Google have catalogue SCIM apps; Entra, OneLogin and JumpCloud use the generic SCIM endpoint (https://api.hubspot.com/scim/v2) via a private developer-platform app with a static token. SCIM deactivates users when removed or deactivated in the IdP; teams cannot be assigned. The user provisioning REST API (create, update, delete users, roles, seats, teams) is on every tier including Free; the audit-log API is Enterprise-only.

plans.name: Professional
plans.price_text: Starts at $90/mo/seat billed annually ($100 monthly) + $1,500 one-time Professional Onboarding

auth.token_source: Okta/Google: OAuth connection from the IdP's HubSpot app; other IdPs: access token on the Distribution tab of a private developer-platform SCIM app
auth.notes: The custom-app token is a 'static' auth app token; expiry is not documented.

endpoints.notes: HubSpot does not publish a SCIM endpoint list; Users is implied by the Tenant URL and user provisioning; group sync must be disabled for Entra and teams cannot be assigned.

roles.how: IdP roles (Okta Roles, a Google custom attribute, or roles from other IdPs with roleSyncEnabled) are matched by exact name to HubSpot permission sets once Permission Set Management is turned on.

limitations.text: Teams cannot be assigned by the IdP; Microsoft Entra must have group sync disabled or provisioning goes into quarantine.
Only one SCIM app is allowed per HubSpot account.
SCIM users can only have permissions edited in HubSpot (and only without permission set management); name and email are IdP-managed.
A verified email domain (DNS TXT record) is required.

endpoints.purpose: Create a user (optionally send welcome email)
Retrieves the roles on an account
Retrieves the seats on this account
See details about this account's teams
Retrieve an audit log of user actions (Enterprise only)

rate_limits.text: Privately distributed apps: Free/Starter 100 requests per 10 seconds per app and 250,000/day per account; Professional 190 per 10 s and 625,000/day; Enterprise 190 per 10 s and 1,000,000/day.

okta.notes: OIN page has SAML, SCIM, Create, Update and Deactivate checked; Group Push not checked (read from page markup).

entra.notes: Gallery app covers SSO only; HubSpot documents Entra provisioning through its generic SCIM endpoint.

onelogin.notes: HubSpot names OneLogin as a custom SCIM integration; OneLogin's catalogue page not checked (bot block).

jumpcloud.notes: JumpCloud's article covers SAML SSO only; HubSpot lists JumpCloud as a custom SCIM integration.

fallbacks.notes: Microsoft's tutorial says provisioning in HubSpot is a manual task for SSO users (no JIT).

conflicts.text: On the seats-based pricing model, the Okta KB article says HubSpot automatically assigns the best available seat when a permission set is assigned through SCIM, while the developer SCIM guide says seats cannot be assigned from IdP permission sets and must be set in HubSpot first.

open_questions: HubSpot does not publish the SCIM resource list, supported attributes, filtering, pagination or PATCH/PUT support.
Whether SCIM deactivation frees the paid seat or ends active sessions is not documented.
Expiry of the custom SCIM app's static access token is not documented.
Whether a seat minimum applies on Professional or Enterprise is not stated on the pricing page.
